tweets.content:
Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
6th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● UAE has moved more crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz than any other producer over the past 2 months.

● Iran and Oman are close to finalizing an agreement on new shipping arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz after more than a month of talks, an Iranian parliamentary official said.

● Iran’s intelligence ministry said that 30 people had been arrested in southeastern Kerman province on accusations including links to Israel’s Mossad and gathering information on military and air defense sites.

● Iran is seeking transit fees between 5% & 7% of cargo values for ships using the strait. Oman wants a lower fee of ~3%, while Washington maintains that no fees should be imposed.

● The IDF struck Hezbollah weapons depots, a command center, and other terror infrastructure across southern Lebanon over the past day.

END OF THE BRIEF

Netram Defence Review (@NetramDefence)

Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
5th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● Commercial vessel traffic through Strait of Hormuz has increased since signing of the now-collapsed US-Iran MoU. Only 731 transits were recorded between the signing and July 29, compared to a pre-conflict average of around 138.

● Houthis of Yemen said they will attack Saudi oil tankers in the northern Red Sea off the Yanbu area after vessels re-routed to avoid the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

● One person was killed and 11 wounded in an Israeli strike on Tebnine, southern Lebanon. The area is separate from where the IDF issued an evacuation notice earlier.

● Iranian and Omani negotiators finalized a draft deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, now awaiting final sign-off from Iran's supreme leader.

● UKMTO reported an incident 95NM southeast of Aden, Yemen. A loud explosion in close proximity to the vessel was heard. All crew were safe, and there was no environmental impact.

● The US Treasury Dept officially lifted counterterrorism sanctions from two aircraft and three airlines tied to IRGC.

END OF THE BRIEF

tweets.title: GAGANYAAN MISSION ON TRACK FOR 2027 CREWED FLIGHT The Government has informed Parliament that India's first crewed Gaganyaan mission remains targeted for 2027, with the first uncrewed experimental mission scheduled for Q4 2026. Developments: - Development and qualification of the Human Rated LVM3, Orbital Module, and Crew Escape System have seen major progress. - The TV-D2 Crew Escape System test is the next major milestone. - Vyommitra, ISRO's humanoid robot, will fly on the first uncrewed mission. - The selected Gaganyatris have completed generic training in Russia and are undergoing mission-specific training in Bengaluru. - The Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) remains on track to become operational by 2035, with the first module already approved. This programme marks a major step toward India's long-term human spaceflight and indigenous space station ambitions.
tweets.content:
GAGANYAAN MISSION ON TRACK FOR 2027 CREWED FLIGHT

The Government has informed Parliament that India's first crewed Gaganyaan mission remains targeted for 2027, with the first uncrewed experimental mission scheduled for Q4 2026.

Developments:

- Development and qualification of the Human Rated LVM3, Orbital Module, and Crew Escape System have seen major progress.

- The TV-D2 Crew Escape System test is the next major milestone.

- Vyommitra, ISRO's humanoid robot, will fly on the first uncrewed mission.

- The selected Gaganyatris have completed generic training in Russia and are undergoing mission-specific training in Bengaluru.

- The Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) remains on track to become operational by 2035, with the first module already approved.

This programme marks a major step toward India's long-term human spaceflight and indigenous space station ambitions.

tweets.content:
BREAKING: Iran Says Hormuz Route Deal Reached with Oman

Iran says it has reached an understanding with Oman on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, with a joint statement reportedly in its final drafting stage.

According to Iranian officials:

- A framework has been agreed on route parameters

- Talks are still ongoing, and no final agreement has been signed

- Tehran says the process could be derailed if "third parties" intervene

While the development could pave the way for easing disruptions in the vital shipping lane, key details remain unresolved, and the U.S. has previously opposed any arrangement that would give Iran control over access to the strait.

BREAKING: India may exchange territory with Myanmar; MEA says proposal under discussion

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has confirmed that India and Myanmar are discussing unresolved sections of their shared border, and a possible territorial exchange in Manipur.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said discussions are ongoing to settle stretches of the border that remain undemarcated, but did not confirm any land-swap proposal.

According to earlier reports, the proposal under discussion involves a small exchange of territory to complete border demarcation between Border Pillars 65 and 68 along the Manipur–Myanmar border.
